examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
Adjacency matrices use Θ(V²) storage and constant-time edge lookup; lists use Θ(V+E) and efficient neighbour iteration. Undirected list representations usually store two entries per edge. Powers of a standard adjacency matrix count walks, which may repeat vertices, rather than simple paths. Directed in/out degrees differ. A representation changes traversal cost even when the abstract algorithm is the same.

**Key relationship:** Matrix space Θ(V²); list space Θ(V+E)

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. State directedness and loop conventions.
2. Count storage and degree contributions.
3. Choose matrix or list costs for each operation.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: State whether the graph is directed and whether loops/parallel edges are allowed. Lists use Θ(V+E) space, with undirected edges normally represented twice. A matrix uses Θ(V²) space and gives constant-time edge lookup. Matrix powers count walks, not necessarily simple paths.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A simple undirected graph has 30 vertices and 75 edges. How many neighbour entries occur across all adjacency lists?

**Answer: 150.** Each edge {u,v} contributes v to u's list and u to v's list. The total is 2E=150 neighbour entries. The 30 list headers are not neighbour entries.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
A matrix-based traversal can take Θ(V²) even when the list-based implementation takes Θ(V+E).

An adjacency matrix can be preferable for dense graphs or frequent edge-membership tests.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

A simple undirected graph has 40 edges. Total adjacency-list neighbour entries?

- **A.** 40
- **B.** 80
- **C.** 160
- **D.** 20

**Answer: B.** Each undirected edge appears at both endpoints, producing 2E=80 entries.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Choose true statements.

- **A.** Matrix storage is Θ(V²)
- **B.** Lists use Θ(V+E) storage
- **C.** Matrix powers count only simple paths
- **D.** Matrix edge lookup is O(1)

**Answer: A, B, D.** Matrix multiplication counts walks with permitted repetitions, so C is false.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

A simple undirected graph on 10 vertices is complete. Number of edges?



**Answer: 45.** Each unordered vertex pair gives one edge: choose(10,2)=10·9/2=45.
